body: On the top-5 of official botanical gardens sadly this comes close to the bottom; above the dismal Hambantota one but below the much newer Seethawaka one (Avissawella). Despite the historic value, with e.g. the first rubber trees, maintenance and staff attitude is underwhelming hence not much fun in visiting:* Two of the greenhouses, for orchids and larger trees, were locked at 11 AM and it took us 15 minutes to mobilise staff that would unlock them, despite the office being a stone's throw away!* The historic rubber tree section has heavy storm damage from 10 years back but was never repaired/modernised* Many of the other sections are underwhelming; yes the palm-fringed entree is great (similar to Peradeniya) but as cars park in the back of the gardens you hardly see it on a usual walking route. Hibiscus section is tiny, the nextdoor fern section is better.* The pond at the back with swan boats is just a nice leisure extension mainly for locals; unlike Seethawaka not integrated in the garden landscape.Hence only recommended for diehard botanical lovers, other tourists better skip these in favour of more time for Peradeniya/Hakgala/Seethawaka.
title: Could have been a lot better

body: Gampaha Henarathgoda garden is extent of 16.93 hectares (43 Acres) of beautiful landscape with a lake developed beside the garden and is situated in 29 Kilometers away from Colombo city. This garden is one of the main centers of ex-stiu conservation of plants in the island. The garden receives an average annual rain fall of 2500mm.There are 1000 to 1200 plant varieties and annual temperature variation is 250C - 320C. The elevation of the henarathgoda garden is about 10 Meters from the mean sea level. Henarathgoda garden was established in gampaha in year 1876 for the purpose of experimentation and promotion of Rubber plant cultivation of Sri Lanka by Dr. George Thwaites, was the Director of Royal Botanical Gardens, Peradeniya. Information gathered by Sampath
title: Gampaha Henarathgoda Garden - Western Province

body: Henarathgoda Botanical Garden in Sri Lanka is a hidden gem waiting to be discovered by plant enthusiasts and nature lovers alike. With over 100 years of history, this botanical paradise boasts a stunning collection of tropical flora and fauna that will leave you awe-struck. As you wander through the lush greenery and vibrant blooms, you'll encounter rare species of orchids, palms, and medicinal plants unique to the region. The garden's tranquil atmosphere provides the perfect escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in the beauty of nature. Whether you're a seasoned botanist or just looking for a peaceful retreat, Henarathgoda Botanical Garden promises an unforgettable experience that will leave you feeling rejuvenated and inspired. Don't miss out on this enchanting oasis in Sri Lanka!
title: Hidden gem waiting to be discovered

body: Established in 1876 by British botanists in order to support their experiments regarding rubber yielding plants in Asia. They obtained seeds from Amazon forests and planted. Experiments were conducted by Royal Botanical garden of Kew. So they did number of experiments both in India and Sri Lanka. Fortunately Sri Lankan experiments were successful. Thereafter Sri Lanka produces very good quality rubber. This garden has dense bio diversity, has excellent variety of trees including bamboo, palm trees, ferns orchids and medicinal plants it is home to many species of birds, reptiles and butterflies. The garden is bordered to Attanagalu river and its intricate water streams. Open to public on Monday to Sunday, 7.30am to 5.00pm. Parking is available. There is a restaurant inside the park but not in good quality. Polythene and plastic water bottles are strictly prohibited. My genuine opinion is the maintenance is really poor. No improvement at all during past few years. Such a great place with great potential is almost neglected. But still this is a good place for a long walk, enjoy nature and to have a boat ride.

body: Henarathgoda Botanical Garden is one of the five botanical gardens in Sri Lanka. The other botanical gardens are Peradeniya Botanical Garden, Hakgala Botanical Garden, Mirijjawila Botanical Garden and Seetawaka Botanical Garden.Henarathgoda Botanical Garden is situated in Gampaha-Minuwangoda main road, 450 m away from Gampaha railway station. It has about 29 km far from the Sri Lanka's commercial capital of Colombo.[1][2] The altitude of garden is about 33 feet above the sea level. It has a tropical low-country climate.The total area of the botanical garden is about 36 acres and, recently it acquired another 7 acres for its expansion process.In 1876 this land was used by British rulers to cultivate Rubber. In later, rubber seeds and plants were imported from Royal Kew botanical garden and planted in this land. This process was supervised by Muhandiram A. De Zoysa, who appointed by British rulers at that time in Sri Lanka.Later this land was transformed in to a Botanical garden. In here there is the first rubber tree in Sri Lanka, as well as some valuable trees from 19th century can be seen.
title: Henarathgoda Botanical Garden
